title: Admit every fixed-width scalar type as a record field
why: W48-QR-SCALAR-TYPES made the scalar_abi table first-class on source.scalar-calls.v1 only (implemented grammars G02t). Record fields (G07.13, `field = NAME ":" "i32"`) are admitted on source.buffer.v1 alone, whose scalar namespace is untyped i32 literals and byte reads, so a typed field would need that route's operands typed too; it keeps its refusal (`let x: u8 = 5;` there is Q051, `x as u8` refuses at the route's own reader). Size: the buffer route's scalar operand reader and binding map (source_std_buffer.rs, source_record.rs, core source_record.rs), the record declaration reader, one C member type per field, field reads rendered through the typed std.io lines; 0 fixtures move. DISCHARGE: `field = NAME ":" SCALAR` with construct-then-read under G02t's typing, checked arithmetic and conversions on the admitting route, Lean parity with QCore.ScalarTypes, native rendering per type.

title: Type the counted loop's bound and index with the fixed-width table
why: W48-QR-SCALAR-TYPES leaves G07.12's `for NAME in 0..BOUND` on source.buffer.v1 untyped: the index is that route's i32-valued scalar and the bound a check-time i32 constant, so a typed bound (a usize extent, a u8 count) keeps its refusal. Size: the loop reader and unrolling (source_loop.rs, core source_loop.rs), the index's type (usize under a recorded target, or the bound's own type), the 4096 ceiling and 8192 event budget restated per type; 0 fixtures move. DISCHARGE: a bound of any integer type with the index at that type, the budget unchanged, Lean parity and native runs per type.

title: Let a bound extern scalar result enter arithmetic, rendering and branches
why: W48-QR-SCALAR-TYPES widened no position whose operand is undetermined at check time. An extern call's scalar result (G02d scalar_binding) can still only be passed on at a declared scalar parameter, and the composed extern + io route (G02i) renders only an i32 whose number a `succeeds INTEGER` outcome declared. Size: the extern route's value namespace (source_extern.rs, core extern_call.rs), the composed route's operand rule (source_composed.rs, Q043 rule 2's one-ABI-width clause), rendering of every ABI width, arithmetic on undeclared results, which needs the typed fault of W48-QR-TYPED-ARITHMETIC-ERROR; 0 fixtures move. DISCHARGE: a bound result of any scalar_abi type is a G02t value on the extern and composed routes, a declared outcome decided at check time and an undeclared one through the typed error, with native runs.

title: Admit every fixed-width scalar type at task workers and copy captures
why: W48-QR-SCALAR-TYPES leaves G02a's leaf-worker parameters and results (i32/unit), `copy` captures and G02j's composed tasks + io operands (a name the task model bound to an i32) at their existing refusals. This is the position track card 3 (task record captures) builds on. Size: the task reader and checked task IR (source_tasks.rs, core task_execution.rs, scoped_tasks.rs), task C emission (task_c_emit.rs), the composed route's operand rule (source_composed_tasks.rs, Q050 rule 3), typed worker results through join; 0 fixtures move. DISCHARGE: every scalar_abi type as a worker parameter/result and copy capture, rendered by workers and parent under G02t, with the task model's trace relation and native runs.

title: Type the Buffer and protected payloads with the fixed-width table
why: W48-QR-SCALAR-TYPES leaves G02b's fixed four-byte Buffer (i32 cells through qcore_buffer_read/write) and G02c's `protected N` payload at i32. Size: the owned-buffer task intrinsics and their C (task_c_emit.rs, mutex_c_emit.rs), the mutex invariant's cell type (mutex_invariant.rs), the CT fixtures pinning four-byte payloads (unchanged unless the width is spelled); 0 fixtures move. DISCHARGE: a payload type named at acquisition or declaration, each cell a G02t value, with the ownership, share and invariant checks restated per width and Lean parity.

title: Carry the arithmetic and conversion fault as a typed error where the checker cannot decide it
why: The user decision of 2026-09-29 (checked overflow) says an operation that can overflow produces a typed error or is refused at check time when the checker can decide it. On every position W48-QR-SCALAR-TYPES widened the operands are check-time constants of the closed evaluation or literal-only folds, so every fault is refused at check time and the emitted guard (exit 86) is unreachable from an admitted program; no error type was added. The first position with an undetermined operand (an undeclared extern result, W48-QR-TYPES-EXTERN-VALUES; a value computed in a worker, W48-QR-TYPES-TASK-CAPTURES) needs the fault as a value: modelled on throws<E>, `?` and `match … Result::Err`, with a named error type (proposed `ArithmeticError` with Overflow, DivisionByZero and OutOfRange variants, or an existing type if one fits). Size: one error declaration, the scalar IR's fault becoming an error exit, the emitted guard returning the error instead of exiting 86, the effect row's throws<E>. DISCHARGE: the typed error on the first such position, Lean parity (a checked operation's None is the error arm), native runs taking the error path at every boundary.

title: Check or refuse parameter type annotations on the sequential route
why: Found by W48-QR-SCALAR-TYPES: the sequential cleanup route (G02) admits a function whose parameter annotation it never reads, `fn g(x: u8) -> i32 { return 0; } fn main() -> i32 { return 0; }` (measured before and after the card, unchanged), so `fn f(x: usize) -> i32 { return 0; }` is admitted with no recorded target although no width is ever given to it. Such a function cannot be called on that route (a direct call must name a zero-parameter function), so no value of the type exists and nothing is emitted for it; G02 already says a structurally accepted spelling is not a claim of ordinary type semantics. Size: the sequential route's function synthesis (driver.rs synthesize_semantics); fixtures with parameterised functions on that route must be censused first. DISCHARGE: a parameter annotation on the sequential route is checked against the G02t table (isize/usize requiring a recorded target) or refused, measured on every fixture.

title: Build the fixed-width helpers natively under MSVC
why: W48-QR-SCALAR-TYPES' native boundary table and rendering runs are Unix-only (Clang 21.1.8 with UBSan). The emitted helpers use explicit range tests rather than compiler builtins so that `cl` can build them, and the renderings use `%zu`, `%td`, `%zX` and `_Static_assert`, which MSVC's C11 mode accepts by documentation, but no MSVC build of a fixed-width program has been run. Size: the two native tests under the existing tests/support/windows_c.rs harness (/W4 /WX); 0 fixtures move. DISCHARGE: the boundary harness and the renderings program built and run under MSVC in Windows CI, each fault exiting 86 and each stream equal to the reference.
